subject: anaesthesia
title: Local Anaesthetic Systemic Toxicity: Maximum Doses, LAST, and Intralipid Rescue

steps.title: Maximum Safe Dosing Guidelines
steps.tx: **Maximum safe weight-based dosages** define upper boundaries to prevent systemic toxicity: plain lignocaine is capped at 3 to 4.5 mg/kg (maximal 300 mg in adults), expanding to 7 mg/kg (maximal 500 mg) when combined with adrenaline (1:200,000). Plain bupivacaine is capped at 2 mg/kg (maximal 150 mg), expanding to 2.5 to 3 mg/kg (maximal 200 mg) with adrenaline, while ropivacaine is capped at 3 to 3.5 mg/kg.

Plain bupivacaine is capped at 2 mg/kg (maximal 150 mg), expanding to 2.5 to 3 mg/kg (maximal 200 mg) with adrenaline, while ropivacaine is capped at 3 to 3.5 mg/kg.

steps.title: Adrenaline as a Chemical Tourniquet
steps.tx: **Adrenaline local vasoconstrictive action** at standard 1:200,000 concentrations (5 micrograms per milliliter) stimulates local vascular alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, producing arteriolar vasoconstriction. This slows the rate of vascular absorption into systemic circulation by 30 to 50 percent, lowering peak plasma drug concentrations (C-max), extending duration of surgical analgesia, and serving as an intravascular test marker.

steps.title: Vascular Absorption Site Hierarchy
steps.tx: **Systemic absorption hierarchy across injection sites** determines peak plasma concentration and toxicity risk according to local microvascular tissue perfusion, remembered by the BICEPS mnemonic: Blood (intravenous) yields immediate catastrophic levels, followed by Intercostal nerve blocks, Caudal epidural, Epidural lumbar, Plexus (brachial), and Subcutaneous tissue, which exhibits the slowest absorption rate.

Lowest peak plasma level; safest site

steps.title: Progression of LAST Symptoms
steps.tx: **Progression of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity** initially displays central nervous system excitation followed by depression, culminating in cardiovascular collapse. Early subjective warning signs include perioral numbness, tongue tingling, metallic taste in the mouth, tinnitus, and auditory hallucinations, progressing rapidly to visual disturbances, muscular fasciculations, grand mal convulsions, respiratory arrest, and coma.

nodes.label: Perioral numbness, metallic taste, and tinnitus
Visual disturbances, dysarthria, and muscle twitching
Coma, respiratory arrest, and refractory ventricular arrhythmias

steps.tx: The order on the timeline is brain first, circulation later. **Progression of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity** begins with central nervous system excitation, moves to depression, and ends in cardiovascular collapse. The earliest subjective warnings are perioral numbness, tingling of the tongue, a metallic taste, tinnitus, and auditory hallucinations. Visual disturbance, muscular fasciculations, grand mal convulsions, respiratory arrest, and coma follow. Refractory arrhythmias occupy the far end, after those neurologic stages.
steps.say: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity starts with central excitation, then central depression, and can finish in cardiovascular collapse. Early warnings are numb lips, tongue tingling, a metallic taste, tinnitus, and heard hallucinations. Visual change, twitching, convulsions, respiratory arrest, and coma come before the refractory rhythm disturbance.

vis.alt: A timeline of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity runs from perioral tingling through seizures to refractory arrhythmias.
vis.caption: Early mouth and ear warnings are followed by convulsions, apnoea, and then cardiovascular collapse that may resist ordinary resuscitation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Cardiovascular Toxicity Patterns
steps.tx: **Cardiovascular collapse in LAST** presents with broad complex ventricular arrhythmias, extreme bradycardia, sinus arrest, progressive intraventricular conduction delays (widening QRS and prolonged PR interval), ventricular tachycardia, and refractory ventricular fibrillation. In bupivacaine toxicity, cardiac arrest can occur precipitously without preceding central nervous system prodromal warning signs.
steps.say: Cardiovascular collapse in LAST presents with broad complex ventricular arrhythmias, extreme bradycardia, sinus arrest, progressive intraventricular conduction delays (widening QRS and prolonged PR interval), ventricular tachycardia, and refractory ventricular fibrillation. In bupivacaine toxicity, cardiac arrest can occur precipitously without preceding central nervous system prodromal warning signs.

left.title: Classical Lignocaine LAST Course
points: Clear progression through CNS warning signs before cardiac arrest
Perioral numbness and seizures precede arrhythmia by several minutes
Wide therapeutic margin between seizure threshold and cardiac collapse

right.title: Fulminant Bupivacaine LAST Course
points: Malignant ventricular arrhythmias can occur simultaneously with seizures
Direct refractory ventricular fibrillation without prior CNS signs
Narrow margin between convulsant and fatal cardiotoxic thresholds

steps.title: Immediate LAST Airway and Seizure Control
steps.tx: **Immediate emergency management of LAST** demands immediate cessation of local anaesthetic injection, calling for multidisciplinary resuscitation assistance, securing the airway with 100 percent oxygen to prevent hypercapnia and acidosis (which worsen local anaesthetic toxicity), and suppressing seizures with intravenous midazolam (1 to 2 mg) or propofol (in small 20-30 mg increments to avoid worsening cardiovascular depression).

nodes.label: Stop local anaesthetic injection immediately and call for help
Secure airway and ventilate with 100% oxygen
Administer IV midazolam or low-dose propofol to stop seizures
Fetch LAST rescue kit containing 20% Intralipid emulsion

steps.tx: Stopping the injection, oxygen and a benzodiazepine for the seizure come first. The specific drug is lipid. **Intralipid** 20 percent is given as 1.5 millilitres per kilogram intravenously, then infused at 0.25 millilitres per kilogram each minute, with further boluses if the blood pressure stays down. The usual ceiling is about 12 millilitres per kilogram. Adrenaline, if it is needed, is kept to small doses because it adds to arrhythmia. Propofol is not a substitute. Its lipid load is far too small, and it depresses the circulation further.
steps.say: Twenty percent lipid emulsion is given as 1.5 millilitres per kilogram, then infused at 0.25 millilitres per kilogram per minute, up to about 12 millilitres per kilogram. Propofol does not replace the emulsion.

vis.alt: Flowchart of the lipid-emulsion rescue protocol for local anaesthetic systemic toxicity.
vis.caption: The rescue sequence gives 20 percent lipid emulsion as a bolus and then an infusion after the airway is secured and seizures are controlled. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Intralipid 20 Percent Rescue Protocol
steps.tx: **Intralipid 20 percent emulsion rescue protocol** is the definitive antidote for local anaesthetic cardiotoxicity. Administer an immediate intravenous bolus of 20 percent lipid emulsion at 1.5 milliliters per kilogram over one minute (approximately 100 mL in an adult), immediately followed by a continuous infusion of 0.25 mL/kg/min (approximately 1,000 mL/hour). For refractory arrest, repeat the bolus twice and double the infusion rate.

rows: Run continuously via dedicated infusion set
Administer up to 2 repeat boluses if pulseless
Do not exceed 12 mL/kg in first hour

steps.title: Mechanism of Lipid Rescue and Resuscitation
steps.tx: **Lipid sink and metabolic activation mechanisms** reverse toxicity through two complementary actions: the lipid sink mechanism creates an intravascular hydrophobic lipid phase that draws highly lipophilic bupivacaine molecules away from cardiac tissue down a concentration gradient. Concurrently, high-dose fatty acids overcome local anaesthetic-induced mitochondrial acylcarnitine transport blockade, restoring ATP synthesis in myocardium.

left.title: Modified ACLS Modifications in LAST
points: Reduce adrenaline boluses to under 1 microgram/kg (under 100 mcg)
Avoid vasopressin entirely; worsens lipid resuscitation success
Strictly avoid class IB and IC antiarrhythmics (lignocaine/flecainide)

right.title: Lipid Sink Dynamic Clearance
points: Absorbs unbound free local anaesthetic molecules from plasma
Accelerates clearance from myocardial sodium channel binding sites
Restores organized cardiac conduction and spontaneous rhythm
